outcomeNote: A mishnaic ruling with an attached a fortiori; no dispute and no dialectical exchange.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ לֹא יִטּוֹל אָדָם אֵם עַל בָּנִים, אֲפִילּוּ לְטַהֵר אֶת הַמְצוֹרָע. וּמָה אִם מִצְוָה קַלָּה, שֶׁהִיא כְּאִיסָּר, אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה ״לְמַעַן יִיטַב לָךְ וְהַאֲרַכְתָּ יָמִים״, קַל וָחוֹמֶר עַל מִצְוֹת חֲמוּרוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «A person may not take the mother» bird «with the offspring even» if he takes the mother for use as part of the ritual «to purify the leper.» The mishna compares the reward for performing the mitzva of sending away the mother bird from the nest to the reward for performing other mitzvot: «And if» with regard to the sending away of the mother bird, which is «a mitzva» whose performance is «simple, as» it entails a loss of no more than «an issar,» i.e., the value of the mother bird, «the Torah says: “That it may be well with you, and that you may prolong your days”» (Deuteronomy 22:7), it may be derived by «a fortiori» inference that the reward is no less «for» the fulfillment «of the mitzvot in the Torah» whose performance is «demanding.»

moves.cueHe: לא יטול אדם אם על בנים
moves.summary: Rules that one may not take the mother bird with her young, even for the leper's purification.
moves.about: the reward the Torah states for sending away the mother bird

moves.summary: Infers a fortiori from the reward stated for this inexpensive mitzva to the reward for demanding mitzvot.
moves.about: a fortiori: if a mitzva costing no more than an issar carries this reward, the demanding mitzvot of the Torah carry no less
